title: AI meal plan generation service: tool-calling orchestration
description:
Create the core AI meal planning service that orchestrates tool-calling with OpenRouter:

System prompt instructs LLM to plan meals by calling tools:
- get_pantry_items: returns pantry items sorted by perishability (HIGH first)
- get_saved_recipes: returns user's recipe collection with ingredients
- get_user_preferences: returns dietary restrictions + cuisine preferences
- plan_meal: called per meal slot — params: {date, meal_type, recipe_title, ingredients[], steps[], source: 'saved'|'generated', saved_recipe_id?}

Flow:
1. Client sends generation config (which days, which meal types) to edge function
2. Edge function builds system prompt with perishability instructions
3. LLM calls tools to gather context, then calls plan_meal for each slot
4. Service collects all plan_meal calls, returns structured meal plan
5. Client processes results — links saved recipes, creates draft recipes for generated ones

Hook: useAIMealPlan() — trigger generation, track progress, handle results

Files: src/hooks/useAIMealPlan.ts, src/lib/aiMealPlanning.ts, src/types/aiMealPlan.ts
Acceptance: Can generate a full week plan via tool calls, correctly identifies saved vs new recipes, respects dietary restrictions
close_reason: Created useAIMealPlan hook with tool-calling orchestration loop. Supports full week generation and single slot regeneration. Handles context gathering, tool call responses, and plan_meal parsing. Typecheck and build pass.

title: Perishability-aware prompt engineering + pantry integration
description:
Design and implement the system prompt and tool definitions for perishability-aware meal planning:

System prompt must instruct LLM to:
- Use HIGH perishability items (Produce, Dairy, Eggs, Meat, Seafood, Bakery) in as many meals as possible
- Spread perishable items across early-week meals first
- Use MEDIUM perishability items (Frozen, Beverages) as secondary priority
- Supplement with LOW perishability staples (canned goods, spices, grains)
- Respect dietary restrictions absolutely (never suggest restricted foods)
- Vary cuisines based on user preferences
- Avoid repeating the same protein/main ingredient on consecutive meals
- Prefer saved recipes that match pantry items over generating new ones

Tool definitions with JSON schemas for:
- get_pantry_items response: items grouped by perishability tier
- get_saved_recipes response: recipes with ingredient match scores against pantry
- get_user_preferences response: restrictions, cuisines, servings
- plan_meal params: structured recipe format matching app schema

Integration with existing utils:
- Use sortByPerishability() and getPerishableItems() for pantry data
- Use ingredientMatcher for scoring saved recipes against pantry

Files: src/lib/aiMealPlanning.ts (prompt templates + tool schemas)
Acceptance: Prompt produces plans that demonstrably prioritize perishables, tool schemas validate correctly
close_reason: Created aiMealPlan.ts types and aiMealPlanning.ts with system prompts, tool definitions, context builders, and tool call handlers. Uses existing perishability utils. Typecheck and build pass.

description:

New pattern for recipes, recipe_groups, grocery_lists, pantry_items:

- UPDATE: same membership check
- DELETE: same membership check

Child tables (grocery_items, recipe_group_items) keep their existing pattern (inherit through parent FK), but the parent's RLS now checks household membership.
